title: A Positive Case for Faithfulness: LLM Self-Explanations Help Predict Model Behavior

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the relative risk of egregious unfaithfulness when perturbing the sex/gender feature in counterfactual inputs to see if models obscure their reasoning about gender.
Measuring the relative risk of egregious unfaithfulness when perturbing the race feature in counterfactual inputs to test if models hide their reasoning about protected racial characteristics.
Measuring the relative risk of egregious unfaithfulness when perturbing the age feature across tabular datasets and Moral Machines dilemmas.
Evaluating unfaithfulness when perturbing 'social value', education level, and occupational features in counterfactual scenarios to see if models hide reasoning based on social status.

Applying the Normalized Simulatability Gain (NSG) metric to the Bias Benchmark for QA (BBQ) dataset to test the faithfulness of self-explanations on questions designed to surface traditional social biases.
